message.text: Looking for the outbound webhook delivery function and its protection against internal network addresses.
Searching the codebase for webhook delivery execution and internal-address protection.
Reading the webhook package and memo_service_webhooks to trace the delivery flow.

The outbound HTTP delivery runs in `Post()` inside `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. It marshals the payload, builds the POST request, and invokes `safeClient.Do(req)`.

Asynchronous deliveries enqueue through `PostAsync` and are handled by worker goroutines in `init()`, but they still invoke `Post()`.

The protection mechanism has two layers. `safeDialContext` in `webhook.go` blocks dialing to reserved IPs via `isReservedIP`. `ValidateURL` in `validate.go` rejects URLs at registration time using `reservedCIDRs`. The `AllowPrivateIPs` flag in `main.go` can disable this entirely.

The final answer cites `Post` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` as the delivery function, and `isReservedIP` / `reservedCIDRs` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` as the protection mechanism.

Outbound delivery runs in `memo_service_webhooks.go`. `webhook.PostAsync` queues jobs to an `asyncPostQueue`, and worker goroutines call `Post()` to execute the HTTP POST via `safeClient.Do(req)`.

Internal network addresses are blocked by `safeDialContext` on the client transport. It resolves hostnames and rejects reserved or private IPs through `isReservedIP` checks. `ValidateURL` also blocks URLs resolving to those addresses during registration. The `reservedCIDRs` constant lives in `validate.go`. A `AllowPrivateIPs` flag in `cmd/memos/main.go` can disable this protection.

The protection mechanism is `safeDialContext` with `isReservedIP` and the `reservedCIDRs` blocklist in `internal/webhook/validate.go`. It enforces the restriction at dial time inside `internal/webhook/webhook.go`.
